data.title: Promise: Review the Companies and Allied Matters Act (CAMA) and other legislations to remove barriers that hinder CSOs from delivering on their mandate.
data.promise_blog:
By prioritizing a review of the Companies and Allied Matters Act (CAMA) and related laws, the HoR recognizes that outdated or overly restrictive legal frameworks can hamper advocacy, service delivery, and civic engagement—calling this a strategic priority by including it in the legislative agenda reflects its importance in reinforcing democratic participation and accountability.

 

The current legal landscape under CAMA poses several barriers to CSOs. For example, the law grants the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) the sweeping power to remove trustees or appoint interim managers in the public interest—without clear due process. This provision gives the government significant discretionary control over CSOs’ governance and continuity. Additionally, cumbersome registration hurdles—such as mandatory government approval of charitable objectives and lengthy publication requirements—delay or sometimes deter incorporation. Removing these barriers would allow CSOs to more swiftly register, operate, and pursue their mandates—particularly in areas like human rights, governance reform, and public service delivery. 

 

This reform is a significant opportunity to strengthen both civic space and checks and balances in Nigeria. For CSOs, a clearer and more rights-focused legal framework would reduce administrative hurdles and the risk of arbitrary interference. This would also make it easier for them to secure local funding and form partnerships.

 

Ultimately, this reform enhances democratic accountability for everyone. By empowering CSOs to effectively monitor government performance, amplify citizens' voices, and drive progress, the House of Representatives demonstrates its commitment to fostering inclusive and resilient civic participation. This makes it one of the most impactful and enabling promises on the current legislative agenda.

HB 659: Companies and Allied Matters Act (Amendment) Bill, 2023 Presented for First Reading 

 

On 19th October 2023, the Companies and Allied Matters Act (Amendment) Bill, 2023, sponsored by Hon. Ozurigbo Ugonna was presented for first reading during a plenary of the House of Representatives.
